content.text: A solution would be, to either return a appropriate error code, e.g. "BAD_ALGORITHM" or to fail the fixity operation entirely (server error).
I started some work here:
https://github.com/claussni/fcrepo4/tree/fcrepo-2400
What is actually the defined behavior for invalid checksums or default algorithms?
Ideally, we should begin moving the Fixity implementation towards the still-draft API specification:
http://fcrepo.github.io/fcrepo-specification/#binary-fixity
That sounds like a good idea. Is the current implementation much different from the specified behavior?
From a code perspective this would also be a good time to re-factor and re-focus the fixity code...
As you know, there are two flavors of fixity:
On-ingest
On-demand
The first is fairly well-aligned with the spec already. The on-demand implementation in the specification is slightly simpler than what we currently have.
I encourage you to be involved in the process for defining the "delta" between the current implementation and the spec:
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/2017-02-10+Fedora+API+Adopters+Guide+Meeting
Thanks for pointing me to the documentation. I will see if I can contribute to the
Fedora Adopters Guide
I'm closing this issue as part of a jira repository scrubbing.  It appears to be out of date, no longer applicable, or addressed by future versions of Fedora.

Given that an unrecognized default checksum algorithm is configured for a resource, a fixity operation returns with "BAD_CHECKSUM" but claims SHA-1 (which is the default) has been used. This might also happen whenever a valid checksum is configured as default (SHA-1, MD5, ...) but no appropriate digest has been calculated for the resource.
See also:
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2297
and
https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2403
